assign.title: Sessions: VS Code tab cost was silently stalling after midnight
assign.outcome:
**Found and fixed the real bug behind the owner's two numbers.** The Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks already logged VS Code sessions' own cost from their transcript (item 1 — landed earlier today by a sibling task) — the gap was that the lookup only ever checked TODAY's date folder, so a tab still open past midnight silently stopped updating. Checked live: session 60d9def6 (this very mastermind's own tab) was stuck at $29.12 while its real transcript already priced out to $110.07.

- [x] VS Code cost from its own transcript via the existing hooks, no timer: already wired (settings.json Stop hook); fixed the lookup bug that made it silently stop working overnight — verified 60d9def6 now reads its true $110.07.
- [x] Fix the roll-up: `week-cost.mjs` now dedupes by session id so two page folders for one session can never be summed twice (checked: no case of it existed yet, but the risk was real and unguarded).
- [x] Recompute usd_per_pct and show its inputs: the "Per 1% of your weekly plan" tile now prints `$claude_usd ÷ plan_pct_used%` under the number, not just in a hover title; real week.json refreshed (usd_per_pct now 19.36, up from the stale 20.04).
- [x] Worktree → review (3 notes, all pre-existing/test-environment artifacts, answered) → merge.mjs, committed to michael/dev.
